Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that there is a positive relationship between aerobic workload and ambulatory blood pressure. Workers who have an elevated relative aerobic workload for several hours each working day are more likely to experience increased risk for cardiovascular disease among those exposed to high levels of occupational physical activity.

In other words, as workers' aerobic demands increase due to prolonged periods of intense physical activity, their blood pressure may also rise. This relationship suggests that addressing and managing the excessive aerobic workload could be an important strategy in preventing cardiovascular disease in workers with this condition.
